name: iTerm2 cmd exec
tile_line: Public exploit: displaying a file runs commands.
tldr: Displaying a crafted file in iTerm2, say with cat, runs commands on your Mac. A full exploit is public; no attacks reported. On iTerm2 3.6.1 to 3.7.8, update to 3.7.9. macOS 12.4 to 12.x has no fixed release.
summary: The trap is hidden in the file, and you only see some shell errors when it runs; it works on a default install, in bash, zsh and fish. The researcher first called it remote code execution (RCE), then retitled it arbitrary command execution; since you have to display the attacker's file, it isn't remote in the usual sense. iTerm2 fixed it on 20 Nov 2026; 3.6.11, the newest release for macOS 12.4 to 12.x, still has the flaw.

affected.label: iTerm2 3.6.1 to 3.7.8
affected.text: The exploit uses Kitty image file transfer, which arrived in 3.6.1 (18 Sep 2025); in 3.6.0 the code for it still returns "Unimplemented". The researcher's write-up now gives the same range, 3.6.1 to 3.7.8. iTerm2 3.6.11, the newest release for macOS 12.4 and later, came out on 2 Jun 2026, before the fix, and has the same flawed code.

affected.label: It shows files from others
affected.text: The file's raw contents have to reach iTerm2: `cat` on a README from a cloned repo or a download is the researcher's example, and any file you might print counts. The hidden part doesn't appear in the output; you only see shell errors when it fires. No setting needs to be changed for it to work.

do.label: Update to 3.7.9
do.text: Choose iTerm2 > Check for Updates. 3.7.9 is a security update: replies iTerm2 sends back to programs no longer include control characters that a shell could run. It also closes the same hole in Kitty drag-and-drop replies (OSC 72) and hardens title reports.

do.label: On macOS 12? No fixed release
do.text: 3.7.9 needs macOS 13 or later, and the 3.6 line (macOS 12.4 and later) hasn't had a release since 3.6.11 (2 Jun 2026). Upgrade macOS if you can; until then, don't print files from others in iTerm2.

do.label: The escape-sequence setting won't help
do.text: The "Disable potentially insecure escape sequences" setting doesn't cover the escape sequence this uses, per the researcher. Updating is the fix.
